📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, creatine is a popular muscle-building supplement, and for good reason. It’s one of the most research-backed supplements for muscle growth and recovery. While some people associate creatine with weightlifters or bodybuilders, it’s a great supplement for anyone looking to build muscle, enhance their performance, and promote better recovery.

In a recent development, there are tons of creatine supplements on the market, including powders, pills, and gummies. These supplements use various forms of creatine (more on that later), and some contain other ingredients that aim to help you grow muscle, recover faster, or sharpen your focus in the gym.

Recent findings suggest that on one hand, having such a wide variety of options can be empowering. On the other hand, it can be a challenge to figure out which is right for you.

To narrow down the field to only the best of the best, our expert product testers tried dozens of creatine supplements ranging from standard powders to convenient capsules to flavorful gummies. We looked for creatine supplements that taste good, mix well (when applicable), use quality ingredients, contain enough creatine per serving, and are affordable. Along the way, we spoke with certified personal trainers and nutritionists for guidance.

It has been revealed that below are our picks for the best creatine supplements for men. However, individuals of any gender can choose from this lineup with confidence.

Industry observers note that disclaimer: While this article is intended for educational and informational purposes, it should not be viewed as a substitute for medical advice. Furthermore, we intend the term “men” to include all men, including trans men. However, we understand most research on this topic has focused on cis men (men who are not trans). When we reference gender-based research and nutritional recommendations, we will clarify by saying “cis men.” We encourage trans and nonbinary people of all genders to consult with a trans-competent nutritionist regarding their supplements and training needs.

Transparent Labs Creatine HMB is our pick for the best creatine monohydrate because it contains 5 grams of it per serving, which is the researched-backed dose for improved athletic performance. “This dose is a great recommendation for the general population, but some sports nutrition recommendations recommend a dosage based on kilograms of body weight, so some individuals may require more than 5 grams to see a benefit,” claims Anna Marie Clear, M.S., R.D., C.P.T.

Recent findings suggest that this dietary supplement contains β-hydroxy β-methylbutyrate (HMB), which the body naturally produces when it breaks down the amino acid leucine. Although more studies are needed, some research suggests HMB promotes muscle growth. “Leucine is the primary amino acid that triggers muscle protein synthesis,” Clear explains.”HMB and leucine are very similar, but research highlights HMB has no greater effect than leucine alone.”.

Transparent Labs also includes BioPerine, a derivative of black pepper that studies show increases nutrient bioavailability. “Bioperine may help enhance absorption of some nutrients, but research is limited on its impact alongside HMB and creatine,” claims Clear.

Earning a perfect formulation score of 5 out of 5 stars, Creatine HMB also received high marks from our testing team for taste. Although it fell shy of another 5-star rating, this supplement earned a solid score of 4 out of 5 in this all-important category.

Transparent Labs Creatine HMB comes in 13 flavors, including an unflavored version. This is a lot more flavor options than you’ll find in most creatine supplements and the most of any on our list.

Pete Nastasi, C.P.T., C.S.N.C., tried this supplement. “I’ve tried both the Blue Raspberry and Strawberry Lemonade flavors, which are sweetened with stevia extract, and both tasted great,” he says. “I love having a flavored creatine supplement in the morning before my morning workout.”.

However, while Nastasi liked the flavor, other testers say this supplement has a slightly bitter taste, which they attribute to the BioPerine.

“I tried Black Cherry and I wasn’t a huge fan of the taste of this one—it tasted a bit watered down, even with the right amount of water,” our product tester noted. “Some people may prefer this though!”.

While another tester also noted some tartness due to the BioPerine, she’s still optimistic about the Tropical Punch flavor.

“I bought this at the end of winter but I’m looking forward to drinking it in the summer because I find something refreshing about it that I think will be nice during the hotter months,” she explained.

Recent findings suggest that we chose Sports Research Creatine Monohydrate as our top pick for athletes because it contains 5 grams of creatine per serving, which research shows is an optimal dose for muscle gain, muscle recovery, and overall improved athletic performance. For this reason, we rated the formulation a 5 out of 5.

Recent findings suggest that this creatine is also a great choice for athletes because it’s Informed Sport Certified—this third party tests for purity and banned substances. So, if you’re planning on competing in any events, you can feel good knowing this product is certified banned substance-free.

Another benefit of this supplement is that it uses micronized creatine. Micronized creatine is ground into finer particles than non-micronized so it dissolves much more easily in water. However, according to Nastasi, “micronized creatine is a bit of a marketing gimmick—it isn’t digested any better than standard creatine monohydrate.”.

Research supports Nastasi, as this 2022 study claims there is “no evidence” that micronized creatine is more bioavailable than non-micronized creatine.

However, using micronized creatine does contribute to excellent solubility. Our tester showed no hesitation giving Sports Research Creatine Monohydrate a 5-star rating in this category.

“If you didn’t tell me there was creatine in this water I wouldn’t know—it’s truly tasteless and mixes easily,” our tester reported.

Unfortunately for your taste buds, this supplement only comes in an unflavored version. However, while some creatine powders can have a bitter aftertaste, this one doesn’t.

It has been revealed that “It tastes just like water,” our tester noted. One thing to consider about this creatine supplement is that it only comes as a powder. If you prefer creatine capsules (or a flavored powder), you’ll want to look elsewhere.

According to recent reports, if you don’t like measuring out and mixing powders, you’re in luck. Swoly Creatine Mono Gummies are ideal for athletes on the go who don’t want to carry around an additional shaker bottle for their creatine.

Although they only come in one flavor (Strawberry), Swoly knocked it out of the park from a taste perspective, earning a perfect score of 5 out of 5 from one of our most experienced product testers.

“These are dangerously delicious — like, need-to-make-sure-my-child-doesn’t-find-these-or-she-will-eat-them all kind of delicious,” our tester eloquently described. “They remind me of the BEST fruit snacks.”.

Concerned about the texture? No need to worry about that, either. Our product tester also gave Swoly a 5-star rating for swallowability.

Recent findings suggest that “Super easy and delicious. I’d eat these every day,” she noted.

It has been revealed that as much as our tester enjoyed chowing down on these creatine gummies, be aware that one serving is five gummies, which can be a lot for some people. Plus, one serving only contains 4 grams of creatine monohydrate, which is a little shy of our preferred dosage of 5 grams. Our R.D. reviewer, Anna Marie Clear, notes that “larger individuals may need to take more of these gummies to get their research-backed dose of 0.1 grams of creatine per kilogram of body weight.”.

If that’s you, you may want to opt for a different option, since taking more than five gummies could “lead to GI symptoms because of the added sugar and gums,” she claims.

Recent findings suggest that unlike some other creatine supplements on this list, Swoly gummies contain more than a few added ingredients, including artificial ingredients. They also have 15 calories per serving and 2.5 grams of added sugar per serving from sucrose, dextrose, and maltodextrin.

As a result, we give the formulation 4 out of 5 stars since we prefer 5 grams of creatine monohydrate per serving and the added sugar may not align with some consumers’ dietary preferences.

Although Swoly notes these gummies are third-party tested, there’s no information about through which organization. As a result, we could only give 3 out of 5 stars in this category.

Sources indicate that if you’re looking for a budget-friendly creatine supplement, you can’t do much better than Nutricost. At just $0.20 per serving, this supplement is the cheapest on our list. But cheap doesn’t equate to low-quality—Nutricost creatine is third-party tested, which is something you typically only find in more expensive supplements.

“This company does not elaborate on its third-party testing,” Clear says. “It’s hard to determine the brand’s safety without a detailed explanation of its testing process.”.

Although we docked a few points for the lack of transparency in third-party testing by giving 3 out of 5 stars, Nutricost earned a perfect formulation score.

“It’s recommended to take 3-5 grams of creatine daily to enhance athletic performance, and Nutricost provides 5 grams daily, ensuring your muscle cells remain saturated,” notes registered dietitian Perry Nix.

Recent findings suggest that our product tester reported no adverse side effects when taking Nutricost. In fact, he was pleasantly surprised that he didn’t experience any bloating like he did with other creatine products.

Another benefit of this creatine supplement is that it comes in five flavor options, which is more than most brands offer for creatine supplements. Flavors include Blue Raspberry, Fruit Punch, Pineapple Mango, Watermelon, and Unflavored. However, these flavors are sweetened with sucralose, which research shows may cause gut complications in some people when consumed in high doses.

One of the few knocks against this budget-friendly creatine is its solubility; or potentially, the lack thereof. Our tester only gave it 3 out of 5 stars, noting that “it settles quite a bit.”.

Industry observers note that amazon reviewers are pleased with this product, giving it 4.6/5 stars overall. Many praise its lack of additional ingredients and effective formula. “It has made a significant positive impact on my workout performance and recovery,” claims Amazon reviewer Kurt. However, a few reviewers mention finding pieces of plastic in their containers, which is something to watch out for.

Sources indicate that some unflavored creatine tastes chalky and a little bitter (no bueno!). If you drink your creatine with water, a flavored option like Legion Recharge should suit your taste buds better. Legion offers this supplement in six flavors, which although not as vast as Transparent Labs’ variety, taste better, according to customers and our team of experts.

Our product tester tried the Strawberry Lemonade flavor, giving it a perfect 5-out-of-5 rating for taste.

According to recent reports, “It’s pretty sweet but also tart. I really liked it” she noted.

In a recent development, many customers on Amazon attest to how good Legion’s flavors are, with a few noting that Strawberry Lemonade and Fruit Punch are particularly good. However, some reviewers mention the Unflavored version has an unpleasant, bitter flavor.

In a recent development, one thing you won’t have to worry about with Recharge is solubility. Our tester reported the power dissolved perfectly with no clumps or sediment at the bottom of her shaker cup, leading to another 5-out-of-5 rating.

Similarly, we’re also big fans of the formulation. Legion Recharge has a research-backed dose of 5g of creatine per serving. The creatine is micronized, which means it’s been processed to be finer. Legion says this makes it easier to blend and less likely to cause an upset stomach. However, our R.D. reviewer Anna Marie Clear notes, “While micronized creatine monohydrate is processed to be finer, the research does not support the micronized version to be more bioavailable.”.

Legion Recharge also contains 2.1 grams of L-carnitine in each serving, which helps the body convert fat into energy, and 10.5 grams of corosolic acid, which research highlights helps regulate blood sugar.

According to recent reports, unfortunately for budget-conscious shoppers, Recharge is one of the more expensive options on this list, checking in at $1.33 per serving. As a result, we could only give it 1.5 out of 5 stars for price. So, if you’re on a tight budget, you may want to go with something like Nutricost.

If you don’t like the taste of creatine powder or find it a pain to mix, Optimum Nutrition Micronized Creatine Capsules are a convenient and tasteless alternative. Plus, a bottle of these capsules will take up less room in your gym bag than a tub of creatine powder.

If you’re trying to achieve some gnarly gains, you can’t go wrong with an affordably priced supplement made with the most widely used brand of creatine. Nastasi agrees: “It’s manufactured in Germany and is super pure, so from a purity perspective it’s no. 1.”.

According to recent reports, gnarly is the only supplement on our list with this form of creatine. According to recent reports, our team tested dozens of other creatines to come up with this list, with many of us relying on some form of this popular supplement for years. However, not every creatine product could make our list, so here are some honorable mentions that didn’t quite make the cut:.

Our team has tried more than 43 creatine supplements in total, with more added on the regular. We evaluate each supplement for the following factors:.

There are a few key factors you’ll want to consider when choosing a creatine supplement.

It has been revealed that research highlights the most efficacious dose of creatine is between 3 and 5 grams for most individuals. Look for supplements with servings within this range if you’re looking for maximum benefits, including increased muscle mass, faster recovery, and improved exercise capacity. Remember, larger individuals may require more creatine for maximum benefits—0.1 grams per kilogram of body weight is the research-backed recommendation.

Some supplements have additional ingredients to bolster the product’s effectiveness. Transparent Labs, for example, includes HMB, which some research highlights promotes muscle growth, though more research is needed. Legion includes L-carnitine, which research shows helps metabolize fat into energy. Consider your goals and whether or not you want a pure creatine supplement or one with other athletic performance-enhancing ingredients.

“I highly recommend collaborating with a sports dietitian to find the most optimal supplement for you based on your personal health, athletic, or physique goals and to ensure you are consuming an appropriate dosage from a safe and high-quality supplement,” says Anna Marie Clear, our expert reviewer and R.D.

Industry observers note that some creatine supplements use artificial ingredients and fillers to help improve taste and mixability. While many of the products on our list contain creatine as their sole ingredient, some, like Swoly gummies, use some artificial ingredients. Consider whether or not it’s notable for your supplement to be completely pure.

Third-party testing is the best way to ensure that your supplement’s ingredients are pure and match what’s on the label. Supplements are not regulated by the FDA, so third-party testing gives consumers confidence in their products.

“It is also especially notable to consider third-party testing for sport certifications from either Informed Sport or NSF Certified for Sport if you are a collegiate or professional athlete or if you are looking to compete in a weightlifting, bodybuilding, or other fitness competition to ensure you are consuming supplements free from banned substances,” says Clear.

Creatine phosphate (CrP) is a compound made of three amino acids: arginine, glycine, and methionine. The body produces creatine naturally in the liver, kidneys, and pancreas, with about 95% of it found in skeletal muscle. “Through diet, creatine is found primarily in red meat and seafood, however, to get an extra creatine boost, a creatine powder or pill supplement can help,” says personal trainer and strength coach Will Duru.

In a recent development, creatine supplies energy to muscles through the phosphocreatine system. “Creatine helps in the production of ATP (adenosine triphosphate)—the compound that provides energy to bodily processes such as muscle contraction,” nutritionist Rob Hobson states. “Creatine can help with the production of ATP during maximum-effort exercises, such as sprints or intense muscular effort lasting between five and 10 seconds. It can also help recovery between exercise bouts.”.

Industry observers note that hobson says creatine can improve performance in sports involving repeated sprints, such as rugby or football, and high-intensity bursts, like track or swim sprints. “Creatine can also help you train harder through being able to do more work over a series of training sets,” he adds.

As a certified personal trainer, former rugby player, and longtime lifter, I can attest to the impact that creatine has on both performance and recovery. It’s been a staple in my supplement stack for years, and despite myths about unwanted weight gain and water retention, I’ve never experienced those side effects.

Industry observers note that as the most-researched supplement on the market, creatine has long been utilized by everyone from professional athletes to strength training enthusiasts to casual lifters. Let’s explore some of the positive potential effects of creatine supplementation:.

In a recent development, “Research reveals creatine supplementation helps muscle performance throughout a number of activities including soccer training, weight training, plyometric training, and even canoe training,” says Duru. Interestingly, this study also demonstrated that muscle power output and muscle strength still increased with creatine supplementation, even when research subjects didn’t do any exercise. This is in comparison to subjects who took a placebo supplement.

“There are lots of studies showing how creatine supplementation can improve strength, power, and high-intensity exercise performance. This is due to the role it plays in energy production and its ability to increase ATP availability during short bursts of intense activity,” indicates nutritionist Rob Hobson.

It has been revealed that want to build muscle? Creatine could be your go-to. “Creatine supplementation is often used to increase muscle mass. It can draw more water into your muscle cells, creating a cell volumization effect that may promote muscle growth,” claims Hobson. “Additionally, creatine can enhance the effects of resistance training by increasing total muscle mass and strength gains.”.

According to a 2023 meta-analysis on the effects of creatine supplementation combined with resistance training, this protocol can promote “a small increase in the direct measures of skeletal muscle hypertrophy in both the upper and lower body.”.

It has been revealed that duru claims for maximum muscle-building results, creatine loading can help. “The first time you take creatine, take around 20 to 25 grams of creatine every day for up to a week, broken up into 5-gram servings across the day. Then drop to the recommended 3 to 5 grams the day after this.”.

Clear adds: “If you are looking to initiate creatine supplementation with a loading dose of 20 grams per day, I recommend breaking this large dosage into smaller servings throughout the day to minimize gastrointestinal distress (i.e., diarrhea).”.

Recent findings suggest that recovery is key when training. Not only does it help you avoid injury, but a speedier recovery means we can get back to exercise quicker. Research indicates creatine supplementation may reduce recovery time between spurts of intense exercise by reducing muscle damage.

Although supplementing with creatine does not entirely prevent muscle damage, studies show creatine reduces the immediate muscle damage that occurs after resistance training.

It has been revealed that studies show creatine can benefit brain function. “Creatine supplementation may have a beneficial effect on brain function, as the brain requires a significant amount of ATP for normal operation. It may be particularly beneficial in tasks requiring speed and quick thinking,” notes Hobson.

Creatine supplementation is also notable for overall health and wellness as you age. According to a 2021 study led by renowned creatine researcher Dr. Darren Candow, one year of creatine supplementation and resistance training had favorable effects on bone area and muscle density in older adults. This included both male and female participants, suggesting no differences between sex when it comes to creatine’s impact.

Industry observers note that not all creatine is created equal. In fact, there are multiple forms. Here’s a brief overview of the different types of creatine so you understand what to look for and what might suit you best.

Creatine monohydrate consists of creatine paired with a water molecule. As nutritionist Rob Hobson notes, this is the most research-backed form of creatine, and it’s typically the primary form used in most of the best-selling supplements in this category.

Industry observers note that “Micronized creatine is processed to create smaller particles than the standard creatine powder,” Hobson says. “The intention of micronized creatine is to improve its solubility and absorption in the body so creatine is then used up by muscles more quickly.”.

In this form, creatine is bound to ester salts, which some studies show makes the creatine more easily absorbed within the body. However, research shows creatine ethyl ester is not as effective as monohydrate.

Recent findings suggest that creatine nitrate is derived from the same molecule as creatine monohydrate but with a nitrate added. Some studies suggest creatine nitrate is more bioavailable than monohydrate, but results are mixed and more research is needed. At the moment, creatine nitrate is only approved by the FDA at a daily dose of 750 milligrams per day.

It has been revealed that this type of creatine is normally manufactured with added alkaline, so it has a higher pH than regular creatine monohydrate. However, research demonstrates there is little difference between buffered creatine and creatine monohydrate when it comes to training gains.

A creatine loading phase involves taking a higher dose of creatine, typically between 20 and 25 grams, for up to a week, according to Duru. He recommends reducing to a dose of 3 to 5 grams a day after a week.

“A lot of people do a creatine loading phase to fully saturate the muscles when they first start taking creatine, and this can potentially speed up the benefits by a few days,” claims Pete Nastasi, CPT, CSNC. “But if you take more than two to three days off from creatine, it’s likely that your creatine stores will go back down to baseline and you might want to do another loading phase,” he says. “That’s why I suggest people take it every day.”.

In a recent development, studies show creatine loading phases (e.g. 20 grams per day for five to seven days) can help increase muscle creatine storage by 10 to 30 percent. However, creatine loading phases aren’t necessary. Studies show that long term, you can achieve the same effects without a loading phase. But if it’s speed you’re after, loading phases are a safe and effective way to rapidly improve gains.

According to recent reports, studies show creatine supplementation is safe in both the short and long term for healthy individuals. Healthy people can safely take up to 30 grams per day for up to five years. However, as we’ll explain below, those with certain health conditions should avoid creatine supplements.

“Since creatine is a safe supplement, there aren’t many precautions to take beyond sticking to the recommended dosage,” says nutritionist Rob Hobson. “Like all supplements, figure out if it is really necessary to suit your performance goals, as there is little point in taking it if it is not. If you are training for a marathon then it’s not really going to be of use to you but if you are looking to build more muscle and become stronger, then it’s a good choice.”.

Creatine works for most people, but those with certain pre-existing health conditions should avoid it. “Anyone with pre-existing kidney or liver conditions or impaired function should avoid creatine,” states Hobson. Experts say creatine supplements may prevent those with kidney or liver problems from producing their own creatine. “Anyone taking medications affecting kidney function should avoid creatine or speak to their GP first. This might include blood pressure medication or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs on a regular basis,” Hobson adds.

According to recent reports, hobson also advises against creatine supplementation for those younger than 18. “With adolescents, while the research suggests it may be okay for this age group, I avoid recommending it as the long-term effects are not fully understood yet,” he notes.

Industry observers note that while myths exist about water retention, cramping, and even its legality, creatine is one of the most researched-backed supplements. If you’re a dedicated lifter looking to enhance your muscle gains, improve your performance in activities requiring short bursts of energy, or hasten your recovery, you shouldn’t hesitate to add one of the options from our list to your stack.

All you have to decide is whether you prefer a powder, pill, or gummy and you’ll be well on your way to unlocking the benefits of this uber-popular supplement.

Micronized creatine is processed to create smaller particles than the standard creatine powder. “Research demonstrates micronized creatine monohydrate is not any more bioavailable than creatine monohydrate itself,” says R.D. Anna Marie Clear.

According to nutritionist Rob Hobson, most people take creatine after working out. “Research highlights taking creatine after your workout may be marginally more beneficial given the increased uptake by muscles during this period, as exercise increases blood flow to muscle tissue,” he says.Hobson recommends taking creatine with a meal or a drink containing carbohydrates. “The effects of insulin help transport creatine into muscle cells,” he says.

It has been revealed that in short, no. According to the International Society of Sports Nutrition, “There is no scientific evidence that the short- or long-term use of creatine monohydrate has any detrimental effects on otherwise healthy individuals.”.

According to recent reports, research demonstrates the best dose is from 3 to 5 grams per day for most individuals. However, as R.D. Anna Marie Clear notes, the research-backed dose of 0.1 grams of creatine per kilogram of body weight means some larger individuals will need more than 5 grams per day to see optimal results.

Creatine may help increase your lean skeletal muscle mass, which can, in turn, increase your overall body weight. This overall increase in lean body mass will likely improve your body composition, as creatine supplementation does not impact your fat mass. “Good quality randomized controlled trials (one week to two years in duration) show creatine supplementation does not increase fat mass. Acute creatine supplementation (seven days) had no effect on fat mass in young and older adults; however, fat-free mass increased.”.

He Ran 3,067 Miles Across America to Set a New Record, Averaging 73 Miles a Day

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1472 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Runnersworld

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, doing his best impersonation of the fictional movie protagonist who developed a passion for running, Balser, a 35-year-old red-bearded and straggly-haired ultrarunner from Indiana, spent the past six weeks spreading messages of love, joy, and kindness on an epic quest to run across the U.S.
  • It has been revealed that averaging about 73.6 miles per day, the Kokomo, Indiana, runner left San Francisco at 5 a.m.
  • His intent was to conclude his journey on the steps of New York City Hall, just as Pete Kostelnick did while setting his TransAmerica Run record of 42 days, 6 hours, and 30 minutes back in 2016.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Forrest Gump has nothing on Cameron Balser.

In a recent development, doing his best impersonation of the fictional movie protagonist who developed a passion for running, Balser, a 35-year-old red-bearded and straggly-haired ultrarunner from Indiana, spent the past six weeks spreading messages of love, joy, and kindness on an epic quest to run across the U.S. in record time.

It has been revealed that averaging about 73.6 miles per day, the Kokomo, Indiana, runner left San Francisco at 5 a.m. PT on October 10 and ran across parts of 11 states before crossing the George Washington Bridge and entering New York City at 11:02 p.m. ET on Friday night. After running a few brisk miles through Manhattan, he eventually met up with his mom, stepdad, and two sisters and slowed to a walk on the final few blocks on the way to his finishing point.

His intent was to conclude his journey on the steps of New York City Hall, just as Pete Kostelnick did while setting his TransAmerica Run record of 42 days, 6 hours, and 30 minutes back in 2016.

The only trouble was that when Balser arrived in Lower Manhattan with a gaggle of two dozen or so friends, family members, and random followers, they found all of the gates to City Hall Park closed and locked. So instead, he walked to a point adjacent to City Hall and, like Gump mythically did in Monument Valley, Utah, he just stopped.

Balser officially ended his relentless push across the country at 11:45 p.m., which means he covered the 3,067-mile journey in a record-breaking 41 days, 16 hours, and 45 minutes—roughly 13 hours and 45 minutes faster than Kostelnick.

“I know it was about the record, but mainly it was about us coming together and being together and loving one another,” Balser told the group around him after he finished. “We shared this experience, and I am so lucky and grateful to be able to do this, and I couldn’t have done it without so many people. I am grateful for this life and I’m going to keep living it like I do. So thank you so much, it means so much to me to have your support.”.

Shortly thereafter, his crew and family members celebrated with some late-night New York pizza and, after devouring a slice or two, Balser almost immediately crashed into a deep sleep.

“And we didn’t set an alarm for 5 a.m.,” crew chief Sam Yeary said.

In a recent development, balser caught the running bug in high school and continued running competitively as a middle-distance runner for Vincennes University. He went through some hard times in his early 20s and dealt with depression that took him to a dark place that had him pondering suicide. But with support from friends, a job as wellness and housekeeping director at the YMCA of Grant County in Marion, Indiana, and an immersion into ultrarunning races from 50K to 100 miles, Balser got a fresh lease on life and has been spreading joy ever since.

According to recent reports, during parts of 2023 and 2024, Balser spent nearly 10 months running the entire perimeter of the U.S. self-supported, covering 11,170 miles at a much more forgiving pace of about 40 miles a day. He built a major social media following along the way, picked up a sponsorship from latest footwear brand Mount to Coast, and started planning the TransAmerica run he claims he'd been thinking about for seven or eight years.

He planned to start in the spring, but his training suffered after he got sick, so he postponed it and began looking for a place to work and train. That’s when Yeary, a friend he met at a few Indiana ultrarunning races organized by Meshingomesia Track Club, offered Balser the opportunity to live, work, and train at his 60-acre family-run regenerative farm near Bloomington.

According to recent reports, training regularly with Yeary, Balser earned some money to help fund his journey, wrangled up a crew of friends and began making plans for October. He knew Kostelnick, a two-time Badwater 135 champion, had averaged more than 72 miles a day in 2016 to shatter the previous record Frank Giannino Jr. set in 1980. Balser decided to commit to running roughly 75 miles a day, which meant 15 to 16 hours on his feet with a rotating crew in a van meeting him about every four miles.

His route closely mirrored Kostelnick’s, taking him across parts of California, Nevada, Utah, Colorado, Nebraska, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Latest Jersey, and New York. He passed over the Sierra Nevada range, across Nevada and Utah’s Uinta Basin, over the Continental Divide at Colorado’s Cameron Pass, and down the Poudre River Canyon, across the Great Plains and through Northern Appalachia, ultimately enduring more than 140,000 feet of elevation gain.

Sources indicate that things didn’t go flawlessly the entire way. He had some stomach complications in late October and suffered from nasal irritation brought on by dry conditions. But for the most part, he was cruising along and following his catchphrase of “movin’ and groovin’” without any major setbacks.

It has been revealed that “It was probably one of the toughest challenges any of us have ever done. It was absolutely insane,” Yeary told Runner’s World early Saturday morning. “We set a big goal this summer when he worked on my farm. We got to think big and dream big. He’s had this on his mind for a long time, but the stars aligned this fall, and we put together a strategy to make it happen.”.

Balser was ahead of Kostelnick’s record pace from the start as his progress was tracked on the Breaking 42 website and Instagram.

He was greeted by supporters at numerous points along the way and often joined by runners who ran alongside him for many miles. Yeary stated Balser and the crew were thrilled, humbled, and grateful to have so many Americans cheering on a couple of Indiana boys.

“Even as a crew, we were blown away by him performing at that level,” Yeary said. “It was hard, but it was necessary for us to treat his consistency for 70-plus miles every day like it was something normal. But we had to in order to keep things going. 70 miles is no joke!”.

In a recent development, balser’s effort developed an inspirational following on his way across the country. Social media engagement spiked over the final days of his quest, and more than 420 people watched his final miles through New York City via Instagram Live. Among those following along and offering support and congratulations on the live stream were U.S. Backyard Ultra champion Mark Dowdle and two-time Badwater Ultramarathon champion Lisa Smith-Batchen.

“As an amateur recreational ultrarunner, I am so inspired,” said Weston Traub, a San Francisco runner who was following along on Instagram as Balser finished. “Seeing him push the limits of endurance reminds me how strong the human spirit is. I have all of these long Strava routes mapped out in my phone that I’ll do ‘someday.’ Nothing crazy like running across the country. Seeing Cam get it done makes me think, ‘Do it now!’ Sometimes next year doesn’t happen, and life gets in the way.”.

Balser wore a YMCA of Grant County T-shirt while running through Newly introduced Jersey and into New York City on Friday night. As part of his Breaking 42 campaign, Balser raised money through a website and plans to give 100 percent of donations directly to that YMCA branch.

“I know people really focus on the record, and, you know, that's a beautiful thing to go out there and set something,” Balser stated. “But the main thing I wanted people to know is just that they're beautiful in the way they are. When we come together to do things, especially if it's something that speaks to our heart and what's possible with that, it's endless, you know?

It has been revealed that “Keep your heart open and find the right people when your head's down to pick you up. I'm truly grateful. I have put my body through more than I probably would want to ever do, but, I know the reach of that, that love. Every step I take, every breath I get to take, it reaches more people, and that's a beautiful thing. And I think it'll ripple through my life and other lives. This record will be broken, but the feeling will last forever.”.

Industry observers note that brian Metzler is a Boulder, Colorado, writer and editor whose work has appeared in Runner’s World, Sports Illustrated, ESPN, Outside, Trail Runner, The Chicago Tribune, and Red Bulletin. He’s a former walk-on college middle-distance runner who has transitioned to trail running and pack burro racing in Colorado.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whether you’re starting your fitness journey or you’re a weightlifting junkie, there are several supplements that should be staples in your stack. As a certified personal trainer and nutrition coach, I’d put a high-quality whey protein powder and one of the best creatines at the top.

Not far behind would be another supplement that can help you achieve your muscle-building and weight-loss goals: pre-workout.

However, just like not all barbells are created equal, neither are supps. The strongest pre-workouts stand out from the pack because they are formulated with research-backed doses of four key ingredients — caffeine (at least 200 milligrams), L-citrulline (at least 4,000 milligrams), beta-alanine (at least 3,200 milligrams), and betaine (at least 2,500 milligrams) — for physical and mental performance enhancement.

Recent findings suggest that to save you the trouble of sipping on something that won’t give you an effective muscle pump, our team of expert product testers tried more than 80 pre-workouts and reported which supplements delivered the most focus, power, and tingles. Then, with some guidance from a few other experts, our squad of CPTs, CNCs, CrossFit enthusiasts, and dedicated weightlifters narrowed down the list to the eight strongest pre-workouts so you can select the perfect match for your goals and preferences.

Medical disclaimer: This content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any new supplement or exercise regimen.

In a recent development, if your goal is to improve your athletic performance and power output in the gym, then we recommend Transparent Labs BULK BLACK. This supplement contains a potent combination of 4,000 milligrams of beta-alanine, 2,500 milligrams of betaine anhydrous, and 10 other active ingredients. Beta-alanine, a nonessential amino acid, may improve potential power output by reducing muscle fatigue, allowing you to push out a few more reps while you exercise. And studies show betaine anhydrous may improve muscular endurance. These ingredients work together to enhance your training, paving the way for strength gains over time.

Each serving of BULK BLACK also contains 350 milligrams of caffeine, which is close to the recommended daily limit of 400 milligrams. Overall, the impressive formulation earns 4 out of 5 stars from our team, as we docked a point for the high caffeine content since it may be too intense for some people.

However, this high-stim pre-workout is certainly effective.

Cory Kessler, C.P.T., C.F.N.C., has tried more than 25 pre-workouts. Cory also experienced the tingling sensation common with high doses of beta-alanine.

Cory also enjoys using BULK BLACK before bodybuilding workouts since it contains 8,000 milligrams of citrulline malate. While more research is needed, some studies suggest citrulline malate may boost exercise and muscular performance.

Two other areas where BULK BLACK stands out: solubility and taste. Our team gave Transparent Labs perfect scores in both categories.

“BULK BLACK completely dissolved in my shaker bottle in only a few seconds with no clumps, grittiness, or residue,” Cory says.

Industry observers note that available in eight flavors ranging from Black Cherry to Watermelon Peach to Strawberry Mango, one of our other product testers chose the Blue Raspberry option, giving it 5 out of 5 stars for taste. However, there are some mixed reviews on Amazon about the taste, depending on which flavor you choose.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s hard to describe the taste of Blue Raspberry, but that’s exactly what it tastes like. Not too sweet, which is a good thing,” he says.

Legion Pulse is our pick for the strongest natural pre-workout because it’s free from artificial sweeteners, flavors, and colors and contains six active ingredients that support enhanced energy.

As a CPT and CNC, I look for four main ingredients in a high-quality pre-workout supplement: caffeine, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and L-citrulline. Each plays a key role in enhancing athletic performance. Research shows:.

Legion Pulse contains all four, including 350 milligrams of caffeine per serving, which is very close to the recommended daily limit of 400 milligrams. Keep in mind that if you decide to try Pulse, it’s a good idea to monitor your caffeine intake from other sources like coffee or tea.

“To get the most out of pre-workout supplements without stomach issues, start with a lower dose to see how your body reacts,” claims Dr. Christopher Mohr, Ph.D., RD. “Choose supplements with fewer stimulants if caffeine bothers you, or go for stimulant-free options.”.

Luckily, if you’re upcoming to pre-workout or are caffeine-sensitive, you can also choose the non-stim version of Pulse. So, even though we’d like to see creatine in the formulation, we still give this a strong score of 4 out of 5 stars, especially since there’s a caffeine-free version.

One of our product testers has tried five different brands of pre-workout and puts Pulse atop her list because of its effectiveness.

According to recent reports, “I’ve been using Pulse three times a week for six months, and it always makes me feel energized and focused,” our tester states. “My goal is to improve my personal records and lift harder, so Pulse is my go-to when I train.”.

It has been revealed that she reports that it typically takes 15 minutes for this high-stim pre-workout to kick in, and while it does give her tingles, it’s not overwhelming. “I never feel a drop-off, but rather a slow energy release,” she claims.

Pulse comes in 22 flavors, including Pink Lemonade, Cherry Limeade, and Strawberry Kiwi, so there’s something to satisfy everyone’s taste buds. That remarked, one of our testers gave Pulse 4 out of 5 stars for taste, noting that while it tastes sweet, there’s a “weird aftertaste.”.

In a recent development, while the formulation and flavor options make this a top-rated pre-workout, Pulse is by no means a budget-friendly option. At around $45 for a 20-serving tub, it earns the lowest score of 1 out of 5 stars for price per serving.

While many strong pre-workouts cost around $2 per serving, Nutricost Pre-X is our pick for the strongest budget pre-workout because it costs less than half of that. At about $0.93 per serving, one tester called it “the best value on the market,” and I agree, giving this a perfect score of 5 out of 5 for price per serving.

It has been revealed that although some budget pre-workouts lack key ingredients, Pre-X contains the four main ones we like to see in a pre-workout: caffeine, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and L-citrulline. “The price is better than most other pre-workouts I’ve tried, especially for a supplement this good,” states one tester.

Each serving of Pre-X has 300 milligrams of caffeine and 4,000 milligrams of L-citrulline, so you should feel energized and get a good pump with this pre-workout. “I got a decent pump and had a calm focus without feeling overstimulated,” one tester claims.

Some testers say Pre-X has a slightly lower dosage of beta-alanine than some other pre-workouts on our list, but others say they experienced noticeable tingles during their workout.

While testers did not experience any negative side effects when trying Pre-X, this pre-workout is made with the artificial sweetener sucralose. Some health experts have raised concerns about taking sucralose in high doses. As a CPT and someone who pays close attention to everything I put in my body, I tend to steer clear of artificial sweeteners. Because of this, we docked a point off the formulation score, giving Pre-X 4 out of 5 stars.

It has been revealed that nutricost Pre-X comes in five flavors, including Blue Raspberry, Peach Mango, and Watermelon. Collectively, our team gave this strong pre-workout 4.5 out of 5 stars for taste.

Sources indicate that “This tastes great ice cold or at room temperature. I look forward to drinking it before my workouts,” states one tester who tried Blue Raspberry.

Another tester who tried Peach Mango also gave Pre-X his stamp of approval.

“No artificial sweetener taste at all. It has a nice flavor that’s not overly sweet.”.

It has been revealed that whether you like a strong pre-workout that’s sweet, sour, fruity, or tart, Jacked Factory NitroSurge has a fit for you. With 11 options, you can stick to your favorite or keep a few flavors in rotation to keep your taste buds on their proverbial toes. Between the deep lineup and satisfying flavors, NitroSurge earned a perfect score for taste.

One of our testers tried Strawberry Margarita, and let’s just say she was more than satisfied with her sipping experience.

Sources indicate that “It’s wildly delicious. I’d drink this by the side of the pool over ice all day.”.

It has been revealed that another tester prefers Jacked Factory NitroSurge to some other strong pre-workouts he’s tried. “I did not like the Pink Lemonade flavor of Legion Pulse, but I would definitely use the Grape NitroSurge again,” he says.

Ultimately, this makes NitroSurge a solid choice for beginners, as you can see how you respond to a single serving before upping it to two scoops.

In a recent development, besides the taste, I like that it’s budget-friendly while still including evidence-backed ingredients, like L-citrulline, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, caffeine anhydrous, L-theanine, theobromine, and AstraGin. AstraGin, also found in Transparent Labs BULK BLACK, is a plant-based compound formulated to enhance nutrient absorption. While AstraGin is safe at 0.5 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day, more research is needed on the potential performance-enhancing benefits.

In a recent development, like some of the other pre-workouts on our list, NitroSurge is made with the artificial sweetener sucralose, which some health experts have raised concerns about taking in high doses. This is especially important for athletes who undergo drug testing for banned substances. We only gave Nitrosurge 3 out of 5 stars in this category since it is made in a Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP)-certified and FDA-registered facility.

For bodybuilders, a “pump” is a sign of a successful training session. Increased blood flow to the muscles makes them feel fuller and appear larger and more vascular during and after a workout. A pump also promotes muscle growth by delivering essential nutrients and oxygen to the muscles as blood flow increases. While you can achieve a pump through high-rep sets, drop sets, and supersets, high-stim pre-workouts like Gorilla Mode are specially designed to improve your pump.

Gorilla Mode contains several pump-enhancing ingredients in each scoop, including 5,000 milligrams of pure L-citrulline (more per scoop than any other pre-workout on our list) and 2,000 milligrams of Hydro Prime glycerol powder. L-citrulline works to widen blood vessels, increasing blood flow to the muscles. Glycerol powder is rapidly absorbed by the muscles and draws in water, which can cause muscle cell swelling.

If you’re caffeine-sensitive or budget-conscious, this intense pre-workout may not be the best for you. Although one serving only contains 200 milligrams of caffeine, you will need to take two servings to get research-backed doses of some key ingredients, including creatine monohydrate (only 2.5 gram per serving). At that point, you’d be at 400 milligrams of caffeine, which is the total amount the FDA claims is safe for adults to consume per day. For this reason, we docked a point off the formulation, giving Gorilla Mode 4 out of 5 stars in this category.

Don’t forget that this also impacts how much bang you get for your buck. A 40-serving tub costs $60, and you’ll end up going through it that much quicker if you take two scoops before your training sessions. That would bring the cost to $3 per serving. So, from a value standpoint, we can only give Gorilla Mode 2.5 out of 5 stars.

On the other hand, this pricey supplement earned a strong score of 4.5 out of 5 stars for its effectiveness. One of our testers uses strong pre-workouts several times a week and tried Gorilla Mode before an upper-body workout. “Not only did I have a good pump, I also felt more focused. I knocked out a few more reps than usual during my workout,” he claims. “I like the Fruit Punch flavor, although it was sweeter than I thought it would be.”.

While our tester enjoyed Gorilla Mode’s taste, he says the powder was gritty and difficult to mix properly. This is likely due to the glycerol powder, which absorbs moisture, leading to clumping.

If you like feeling skin tingles after taking your pre-workout, check out Crazy Nutrition Intensive Pre-Train. I love the prickly skin sensation because it lets me know my pre-workout is kicking in and it’s time to train. This temporary side effect, called paresthesia, is caused by beta-alanine, which works to increase muscular endurance.

Intensive Pre-Train has 3,500 milligrams of beta-alanine per serving, which is more per serving than almost all of the other pre-workouts on our list. “Beta-alanine is found in most pre-workout supplements, likely because it helps reduce fatigue and improve endurance in the short term,” indicates registered dietitian Alex Oskian. “This is because it reduces acidity in the body, which comes from lactic acid build-up.”.

According to recent reports, our product tester used Crazy Nutrition Intensive Pre-Train before a high-intensity interval training (HIIT) workout and felt the tingles within 15 minutes. “These were strong compared to some other pre-workouts I’ve tried,” he says. “I felt good tingles in my hands and face, which lasted for about an hour.”.

Earning a 5 out of 5 for effectiveness, Intense Pre-Train is also available in a caffeine-free version for those who don’t want stimulants in their pre-workout. The non-stim version comes in Green Apple, which our tester says tasted more like a greens powder than a sour apple.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m rather caffeine-dependent, so I didn’t feel a burst of energy. I prefer caffeinated pre-workouts, but this is a great option for a late-night lifting session,” she indicates. Other testers who tried the Fruit Punch flavor say they enjoyed the tangy taste. To enhance the flavor, Crazy Nutrition is sweetened with the artificial sweetener sucralose. With some mixed reviews on the different flavors, we give this pre-workout a 3.5 out of 5 for taste.

Industry observers note that onnit Alpha Brain is designed to increase mental acuity and focus. Testers say that’s exactly how they felt after trying Onnit Alpha Brain, which is why it’s our pick for the strongest pre-workout for focus.“What makes this pre-workout stand out is the cognitive effects. I felt significantly more focused after taking Alpha Brain than any other pre-workout I’ve tried,” says one of our testers.

Other testers agreed, saying Alpha Brain helped them feel present and ready to work out without being overstimulated, leading to an effectiveness score of 4 out of 5 stars.

Sources indicate that onnit Alpha Brain’s formula differs from most other strong pre-workout supplements on our list — it contains nootropics, substances that enhance learning and memory. One of the key ingredients, NooGandha, is an ashwagandha extract that can reduce stress and enhance well-being by reducing cortisol levels in the body.

Another key ingredient, AlphaSize, may promote the production of acetylcholine, a powerful neurotransmitter that enhances cognitive function. However, studies demonstrating the effect of alpha-GPC on cognitive performance used 200 to 400 milligram doses per day, and a serving of Onnit Alpha brain has 125 milligrams.

It has been revealed that the other unique ingredient in Onnit Alpha Brain is Dynamine. It works similarly to caffeine, by blocking the body’s adenosine receptors that cause you to feel tired. However, this ingredient is banned in all sports supplements in Australia. While Dynamine is still allowed for sports competitions in the U.S., it is possible it will be banned in the future. Competitive athletes may want to steer clear of this product.

One of our testers states Alpha Brain is only middle-of-the-road compared to other strong pre-workouts when it comes to physical energy. “After taking other strong pre-workouts, I usually experience a boost in energy. After taking this pre-workout, the mental effects were much more noticeable than the physical ones,” she says. That may be in part because Alpha Brain lacks ingredients like betaine anhydrous, taurine, and creatine, which can support muscle growth and recovery.

We give the formulation 4 out of 5 stars thanks to the inclusion of nootropics, which are quickly becoming more prevalent in the supplement market. But be aware that this probably isn’t your best bet for boosting your physical energy levels.

Long before the days of gummy and ready-to-drink (RTD) pre-workout options, the most popular choice was the original C4. The latest version, C4 Ultimate, is more concentrated than the classic formula, combining both exercise performance and cognitive-enhancing ingredients.

One of our testers tried C4 Ultimate before a 30-minute HIIT workout, reporting that the caffeine blend got her zoned in before her training.

“I felt great throughout the entire workout,” she reported, giving C4 Ultimate a perfect score for effectiveness.

Industry observers note that this high-stim pre-workout is sweetened with sucralose, which some health experts have raised concerns about. While our tester doesn’t mind a very sweet pre-workout, the Icy Blue Razz flavor was a little too sugary for her liking. Mixing it in more water than recommended balances out the sweetness.

However, another tester was blown away by the Sour Batch Bros flavor, saying it tasted “just like Sour Patch Kids.” Taking both of their experiences into consideration, we’ll meet in the middle and give C4 Ultimate a 4 out of 5 for taste, especially since it comes in multiple flavors.

In a recent development, another plus for this product: It contains creatine — a popular supplement among athletes and bodybuilders for its ability to boost strength, enhance recovery, and prevent injury. Because of its performance-enhancing capabilities, some people like to take creatine in addition to their pre-workout. If you want the best of both worlds, we recommend C4 Ultimate.

Keep in mind that one serving contains 1.5 grams of creatine per serving, which is less than the recommended value of 3 to 5 grams daily. If you want to get the most performance-enhancing benefits from creatine, you should invest in a standalone supplement to help support your fitness goals.One final note: If you compete in a sport that requires drug testing, C4 Ultimate may not be the best strong pre-workout for you because it’s made with Dynamine, which is currently banned for use in Australia.

Sources indicate that our team of expert testers includes certified personal trainers, nutrition coaches, and CrossFit enthusiasts. As dedicated lifters and lovers of all things health and fitness, we’ve collectively tried more than 80 pre-workouts, giving us a broad perspective of what’s available on the market.

We tested each supplement before a workout, and in some cases, for several weeks or months, to evaluate its performance-enhancing benefits, taste, and whether the supplement had any negative side effects.

Using a 1-5 scoring system, we rated each pre-workout on a variety of factors, including:.

Recent findings suggest that at the end of the testing period, we compared feedback to whittle our list down to only the best of the best. We also received valuable input from nutrition experts on what makes a strong pre-workout.

A strong pre-workout contains a combination of performance-enhancing ingredients in research-backed dosages. “Usually, the strength of a pre-workout is based upon the amount of stimulants it contains. High doses of caffeine (300+ milligrams) are usually a quick identifier of the pre-workout’s strength,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian says.

Recent findings suggest that however, the potency of a pre-workout goes beyond the caffeine content. Other active ingredients like L-citrulline, beta-alanine, and betaine anhydrous can impact energy, focus muscular endurance, and power output.

Sources indicate that “Stronger via the amount of caffeine isn’t always better. If the goal is a bigger pump in the gym, other ingredients like L-citrulline may be better,” says Alex. “Another common ingredient that can help a pre-workout feel stronger is beta-alanine, which may cause a tingling or ‘pins and needles’ sensation on the skin.”.

Sources indicate that it’s also vital to remember that “strong” is a subjective term. For example, I can handle a full scoop of RedCon1 Total War without a problem, but I have friends who get too many tingles from a single serving.

Sources indicate that “Everyone’s body reacts differently to various compounds, so what works for one person might not be best for another,” states Dr. Christopher Mohr, Ph.D., RD.

A strong, well-dosed pre-workout supplement may help you train harder by boosting your energy, focus, and endurance during intense workouts.

“There are a few things that are really helpful when you are looking for a great gym session: energy to do the work, mental clarity to help focus on what you are doing (not just to work the muscle, but to prevent injury), and a great workout,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian states. “Using a pre-workout may just help you achieve all of these.”.

Let’s explore the potential benefits of taking a strong pre-workout before you start your training session.

Sources indicate that caffeine is one of the most popular stimulants used in pre-workout supplements to enhance energy levels and improve focus. Almost all of the pre-workouts on our list use caffeine and L-theanine. Studies have shown when paired with caffeine, L-theanine may improve cognitive performance.

“Most pre-workouts contain the stimulant caffeine in higher dosages. L-theanine helps counteract the unwanted effects of caffeine supplementation: jittery feelings and a post-caffeine crash,” Alex says. “You might see less mental fatigue, improved reaction time, and fewer headaches while regularly supplementing with L-theanine.”.

I like taking a pre-workout to improve my focus because it helps intensify my workout and keep me #lockedin. Several pre-workouts on our list contain Alpha-GPC and tyrosine to give you that zoned-in feeling. Research suggests Alpha-GPC may improve cognitive function, and tyrosine may increase dopamine levels and cognition. One study found L-tyrosine helped improve people’s memory while they worked on a demanding task.

A pre-workout may help you squeeze out a few more reps as you work to build strength and muscle. Two ingredients commonly used in pre-workout, beta-alanine and betaine anhydrous, may help reduce fatigue and support muscular endurance.

Sources indicate that “Research suggests betaine anhydrous can improve muscle strength and power via increased total work capacity and improved protein synthesis within the body. Simply put, you can do more work, which leads to increased strength and muscle growth,” states Alex.

Another common ingredient, taurine, may improve your performance and power.

Registered dietitian Alex Oskian claims not every pre-workout is created equal, so it’s important to pay attention to what’s on the label. “Supplements are not regulated by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This means the supplement might not contain all the ingredients you’re looking for and may even contain unwanted ingredients,” she says. Alex recommends looking for supplements that undergo third-party testing.

Industry observers note that if you choose a high-stim pre-workout, be mindful of your caffeine intake from other sources like coffee, tea, or soda so that you don’t go over the daily recommended value of 400 milligrams. This will help prevent potential negative side effects like jitters, anxiety, or trouble falling asleep.

“Consuming caffeine at the end of your day may cause sleep disturbances, which only hurts performance in the long run,” says Oskian.

In a recent development, no matter which pre-workout you choose, it’s notable to follow the recommended intake guidelines. Remember, pre-workouts should not be taken more than once per day.

In a recent development, “Pre-workout supplements are generally safe for healthy adults, but they can have some potential side effects,” notes Dr. Raj Dasgupta, MD, FACP, FCCP, FAASM. “It is important to start with a low dose and talk to your doctor before taking them, especially if you have any underlying health conditions.”.

There are a number of important factors to consider when deciding which strong pre-workout is right for you, including:.

Recent findings suggest that many strong pre-workouts incorporate a variety of active ingredients. When choosing a pre-workout supplement, consider your goals. For example, a bodybuilder may prefer a pre-workout powder that’s highly caffeinated and contains ingredients such as L-citrulline, betaine anhydrous, and creatine to help improve performance. On the other hand, an endurance athlete may want a pre-workout that has less caffeine but includes beta-alanine, BCAAs, and mineral electrolytes.

It has been revealed that whenever possible, I choose supplements that are tested by a third party for purity and have transparent labeling. Athletes who undergo drug testing should look for certifications from Informed Choice and NSF, which ensure the product does not include any banned substances.

Sources indicate that although we test all of the products we recommend, it’s important to check out customer reviews, especially from people with similar fitness goals and preferences. They can provide valuable insights into the product’s overall effectiveness, potential side effects, and the most popular flavors.

“Recommended brands and products are ones that are highly rated by consumers and contain ingredients that have been backed by scientific research,” indicates Dr. Raj Dasgupta.

Industry observers note that “Taste plays a big role in pre-workout selection. If you don’t like a particular flavor, then you likely won’t drink the pre-workout no matter its benefits,” Oskian states. It’s also key to consider the use of artificial flavors, colors, and sweeteners.

The price of a pre-workout doesn’t necessarily reflect its effectiveness. Understanding the ingredients list and dosage levels is important to ensure you’re paying for a high-quality supplement and not just expensive marketing.

There are a few potential red flags you want to avoid when picking out a pre-workout.

According to recent reports, I like to avoid supplements made using proprietary blends. These blends are combinations of ingredients, but the individual doses are not fully disclosed. This lack of transparency makes it impossible to assess the effectiveness and safety of the supplement.

Industry observers note that many fitness enthusiasts and athletes prefer all-natural ingredients and products free from unnecessary fillers or additives. “If sugar alcohols and artificial sweeteners wreak havoc on your stomach, make sure those aren’t on the ingredient list,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian says.

Athletes who compete in sanctioned organizations should make sure the supplements they use are third-party tested and certified banned substance-free.

If you have big fitness goals, choosing a strong pre-workout formulated with safe and effective doses of science-backed ingredients is worth it to deliver performance-enhancing effects. Keep in mind that even the strongest pre-workouts on the market won’t make you run faster, lift heavier, or exercise longer on their own. These supplements are designed to help you put in the work at the gym to make gains and enhance your performance over time.

Recent findings suggest that ultimately, though, a strong pre-workout is only part of the equation to becoming the strongest version of yourself. At the end of the day, you have to put in the work, follow a sound nutrition initiative, and prioritize rest and recovery to crush your fat-burning and muscle-building goals.

Yes, technically, you can take a pre-workout made with 400 milligrams of caffeine. However, that is the maximum daily dose recommended by the FDA. This means if you’re using a high-stim pre-workout, you may want to avoid caffeine from other sources like coffee, tea, soda, or energy drinks. Since 400 milligrams is the maximum recommended daily dose, I do not advise using a pre-workout containing 600 milligrams of caffeine.

Sources indicate that A pre-workout can directly and indirectly make you stronger. A well-dosed pre-workout may help you add a few pounds to your lifts or allow you to push out a few more reps during your workout. However, real strength gains will come from consistent training, proper nutrition, and recovery. If a pre-workout supplement helps you stay consistent in the gym, it may also help you gain strength and muscle mass.

In a recent development, yes. Depending on your sensitivity to stimulants like caffeine, you may experience side effects, including jitters, anxiety, or difficulty falling asleep. If this is the case, use a half serving or a more moderately dosed pre-workout to assess your tolerance.
